newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon has funds to cover budget deficit-c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon has funds to cover budget deficit-c.bank.

text.p: The Lebanese government has sufficient surplus in its creditor account with the central bank to cover the projected 1997 budget deficit, Bank of Lebanon Governor Riad Salameh said on Monday.

"I can tell you that the Lebanese government is running a sufficient surplus in its creditor account at the central bank, therefore there is no need to issue more treasury bills than those that are maturing," Salameh told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"We don't need a surplus because the level of the creditor account of the government is sufficient to cover all the projected (budget) deficit for the coming year," Salameh said.

He was replying to questions after the central bank for the first time imposed limits on the amount of t-bills awarded to non-competitive bids, made by private individuals and foreign investors, at the weekly auction of three- and six-month t-bills on Saturday.
Salameh said the central bank's policy included stabilisation of t-bill interest rates at around their current level following their decline in recent months.
